_comment: GENERATED by scripts/gen-device-policy.js — DO NOT EDIT.
Every combination of (scope, locked, mode) and the exact argv a remote
request must turn into. Both runners are tested against this file, so a
change here is a change to what a request may do to somebody's computer;
read the diff, do not just regenerate it.
argv omits --model/--effort/--resume/--append-system-prompt: those ride along
unchanged whatever the scope, and are covered by DevicePolicyTest.
A refused case still carries an argv on purpose. The refusal is the first
fence and the runner never spawns — but if it ever did, the argv it would
have used must still be the read-only one. Two fences, both asserted.
Modes nobody defined (constructor, __proto__, "") are here deliberately:
they are inherited properties of any plain object, so a table built from
JSON answers them with a function, and one runner read that as "allowed at
every scope". Every row for them must be a refusal.
Scopes nobody defined (root, constructor, "") floor to SCOPES[0] = generate
in all three programs, so their rows must match the scope-generate rows
exactly: nothing a claude device runs, and only an llm engine ever serves.
A GRANTED generate row is the bare streamFlags — no tool flags at all, and
--effort/--append-system-prompt are stripped for generate mode too (that
half is asserted per-runner, since the matrix argv omits ride-alongs).
A REFUSED generate row carries the look argv, per the two-fences rule.
